description: The papers that one paper cites, which is the other half of the citation graph that find_citing_papers covers. Every result carries a one line abstract, so you can judge a paper before you open it. Use it to read the bibliography of a paper, to find the source a result came from, or to work backwards from a paper to the earlier work it builds on. A showing line says which references are on this page and how many the paper lists in all, with the page to ask for next. Inputs: paper (required, a DOI like 10.1038/nature14539, a doi.org link, or an OpenAlex id like W2741809807), sort (optional, cited_by_count:desc for the most cited references first, or publication_year:asc for the oldest references first), page (optional, which page of results to show, 1 to 400, 1 by default), limit (optional, 1 to 25, default 8). Example prompt: 'what papers does DOI 10.1038/nature14539 cite?'

limit.description: How many results to return, 1 to 25.

page.description: Which page of results to show, 1 to 400, 1 by default. Pass the page the showing line names to read the next page.

paper.description: A DOI like 10.1038/nature14539, a doi.org link, or an OpenAlex id like W2741809807.

sort.description: How to order the references. cited_by_count:desc puts the most cited references first, publication_year:asc puts the oldest references first.

name: paper_references
title: Paper references
